scenes.summary: How this is counted · specialization_exposure_v2 · forearm_mappings_v2
scenes.notes: Each catalog exercise the forearm atlas maps has one default variant (cat-<id>) with its execution spelled out: organization, forearm orientation, wrist position, grip, straps, laterality, measure, deliberate hold, and an elbow angle only where the exercise defines one. Each mapping names one muscle, one joint action, a relationship (direct, contributing, stabilizer, incidental) and a muscle mode (dynamic or isometric) separately, so one set can be dynamic elbow flexion and isometric wrist stabilization at once. Mappings are by catalog id; no name matching. A mapping is reviewed when the muscle's action is sourced (anatomy tables S4, S7, S8, the arm reference M8) and the relationship is explained in its rationale; EMG sources (S2, S3, M1, M2, M5-M7) are cited only for what they measured. Everything else stays draft and is shown as pending review, never counted. FDS and FDP are always credited together as shared: nothing in an ordinary grip separates them. Grip during rows, pulldowns, pull-ups, deadlifts, shrugs and hangs is incidental and is not earned by a set logged with straps. No percentage splits between muscles, no mapping credits every forearm muscle, the hand's own muscles are not credited to the forearm, and a broad 'forearms' tag on an unmapped exercise stays region-level. Version 2 reviews the thumb flexor's role in hangs and carries as incidental grip, adds the wrist extensors and flexors steadying the wrist in grip holds, carries and the gripper, the pronator quadratus steadying the joint near the wrist in lever supination, and the brachioradialis in face pulls and cable rows, and maps four new exercises. Its new EMG sources (pmid.9503091, pmid.14656682, pmid.32636008, pmid.35646483) are cited only for which muscles they found active. It adopts none of the research package's grades or percentages. It credits no upper-arm muscle: the upper arm's own version does.
